subject: OrchidAI production: elevated latency & errors — exec escalation
messages:
From: Alex Doyle <adoyle@orchid.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: sudden spike in latency and error rate to Redwood endpoints

Hi Rachel —

Heads up: starting ~08:48 PDT we see a sharp degradation for calls to redwood-infer.orchid (our integration). Symptoms: p50 has jumped from ~45ms to ~620ms, p95 up to ~1.3s, overall error rate ~12% (5xx and timeouts). Throughput for the integration dropped ~40% because our clients are backing off. We confirmed this is not a code push on our side.

Attached is a short sample of errors from our side (orchid_errors.log) and a couple of request ids. Can you confirm if there are any ongoing infra changes or incidents on your side? We rely on these endpoints for inference in production for our real-time feature. This is impacting customer-facing SLAs.

Requesting immediate assistance and a bridge if possible.

— Alex
VP Product — OrchidAI

Attachments: orchid_errors.log (text)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Doyle <adoyle@orchid.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden spike in latency and error rate to Redwood endpoints

Alex — thanks for the alert and the logs. We’re looking immediately.

Quick asks while we triage:
- Can you share traceroutes or the request ids for a sample failing call (we have a few already from your log).
- Are you routing through a customer-managed proxy/VPN for calls to our hosted endpoints?
- Which region/edge are most of your calls coming from (I see a mix but want a primary region)?

I’m looping in Sean (SRE) and we’ll open a bridge. If you can, please open a parallel ticket with your cloud provider with the attached ids — we’ve seen peering/DNS-related issues cause similar symptoms.

We’ll update within 30 mins with an initial diagnosis.

— Rachel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:36:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: OrchidAI prod latency — potential VPC peering/DNS/proxy path issue (impacting traffic)

Team — short summary: OrchidAI reports a production-wide latency spike and 5xx/timeouts starting ~08:48 PDT. Their metrics: p50 ~620ms, p95 ~1.3s, error rate ~12%, throughput -40%. This affects ~50% of their traffic to our hosted US-west endpoints.

What we’ve collected so far:
- Orchid provided request ids and a sample log (attached).
- Our edge telemetry shows a surge of SYN retries and TCP retransmits from their ASN range 39712.
- DNS: multiple NXDOMAIN/servfail spikes reported from their resolver cluster for our API hostname during the event window.
- No deploys on our side at the time. No scheduled infra changes.

Preliminary hypothesis: asymmetric routing or an intermediate customer proxy/firewall (or cloud provider route flap) is causing connection establishment delays + DNS instability so some calls fail and others shoot to fallback paths that increase RTT. This fits a pattern we’ve seen when VPC peering prefixes exceed route table limits or when corporate proxies inject connections through an inspection appliance.

Immediate asks / mitigation options:
1) Engineering (Jonas): can you pull tcpdump/syn logs for the Orchid ASN and look for asymmetric src/dst IPs and TTL discrepancies?
2) SRE (Sean): can we temporarily route Orchid traffic to our US-east fallback pool (force-region) to reduce impact if routing is the cause? That would take ~20-40 mins to spin up routing and LB changes.
3) Commercial (Marissa): prepare customer communication and offer a short credit if slippage persists.
4) Exec (Markus): flag for potential escalation — this is causing visible customer pain for a top-10 account and risks renewal. We may need permission to authorize credits or to open an escalated support case with the cloud provider on behalf of Orchid.

I attached a small trace bundle we’ve pulled from our edge (traces.zip). I’ll post updates as we have telemetry.

— Rachel

Attachments: traces.zip (tar.gz of spans)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: OrchidAI prod latency — preliminary edge traces

Quick technical readout from edge team:
- Captured tcpdump for a 10-minute window shows a high rate of SYN->SYN-ACK retransmits to our API VIPs originating from Orchid's peering range. Latency spikes correlate with windows where SYNs are retried 3-4x before connection establishment.
- We also see that a subset of requests resolves to a private VIP (internal load balancer address) that should only be reachable inside a VPC. That points to either misconfigured DNS (split-horizon) on their side or an intermediate resolver returning stale/private answers.
- Firewall/proxy evidence: HTTP/1.1 requests intermittently include Via/Forwarded headers indicating an inspection appliance in the path. When those headers are present, latency is ~2-3x higher.

Likely root causes (not mutually exclusive):
1) VPC peering route table constraints or recent route propagation resulting in asymmetric routing.
2) Customer-side DNS resolver returning private/internal records for our public hostnames.
3) On-path inspection/proxy adding RTT and occasional connection drops.

Recommended immediate action:
- Sean: trigger failover to US-east pool for Orchid traffic and publish a short TTL (~60s) DNS override from our side for their client IP ranges to point to the east pool. This buys time while they (or we) coordinate with their cloud provider.
- Rachel/Marissa: tell customer we’re executing a region failover now and will confirm once traffic normalizes.

Estimated time to mitigation: 30-90 minutes (depending on DNS TTL propagation and edge routing convergence). If we need to push a BGP fix with their provider, that could be multiple hours.

— Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Exec brief: OrchidAI outage impact & request for emergency authorization

Markus —
We have a high-impact production issue affecting OrchidAI (top-10 account). Summary:
- Impact: ~50% of Orchid traffic to our US-west hosted endpoints is experiencing high latency and ~12% error rate since 08:48 PDT. Customer reports partial service degradation and user-facing errors.
- Likely causes: VPC peering/route propagation issue, customer DNS returning private VIPs, and on-path inspection proxies increasing RTT. Edge traces attached confirm SYN retransmits and Via headers.
- Mitigation in progress: engineering recommends failing traffic to US-east pool and applying a short-TTL DNS override for Orchid client CIDR ranges. Estimated mitigation timeframe: 30–90 minutes.

Asks:
1) Authorization to execute emergency routing and DNS override for Orchid (risk: temporary regional imbalance in our backend costs).
2) Approval to offer a service credit if SLA targets miss for their billing window. Commercial asks a quick green light to offer up to a 10% credit pre-approved to avoid delay.
3) Approval to open an escalated support engagement with their cloud provider (we may need to share network packet captures).

Business risk: Orchid runs a recently-signed expansion deal (RDW-67890). Continued instability risks churn and exec escalation on the customer side.

Please reply with approval or a quick call window — time is material here.

— Rachel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Doyle <adoyle@orchid.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <mruiz@orchid.ai>, CloudOps Support <support@bigcloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec brief: OrchidAI outage impact & request for emergency authorization

Rachel / Markus / team —
Thanks for the rapid response and clear mitigation steps. We’ve opened a concurrent support ticket with our cloud provider and shared the tcpdump excerpts and request ids (ticket #CB-33211). CloudOps confirmed they see route flaps in our peering table and are engaging their networking team.

We approve your proposed failover to US-east for our client CIDR ranges — please proceed. We will also provide network-dump.pcap from our side and the traceroutes you requested.

Appreciate the urgency. Please keep us posted on the timeline for full resolution and any credit offer.

— Alex
VP Product — OrchidAI
